verified.notes: NASA.gov press release, fetched 200. Numbers (33M L, $1.07B) supported at the stated basis. Stored excerpt condenses four individually-verbatim sentences — faithful. Correctly a NASA (not SpaceX-specific) sole-source contract; used for the concentrated launch-helium structure + Air Products' role.

USGS MCS 2024 helium PDF. WebFetch rendered binary as flagged; re-fetched fresh via curl (HTTP 200, 777722 bytes, intact — not a JS shell) and extracted text with pypdf from the OFFICIAL PDF (not a reconstruction). Numbers exact. Both sentences verbatim: 'Linde today announced it has signed another long-term agreement with a major space launch company in Florida' and 'Linde will supply the customer with liquid oxygen and nitrogen from its air separation plant at Mims, Florida.' CONFIRMED: the word 'SpaceX' does NOT appear on this primary page; customer is 'a major space launch company' / 'the customer' only. No numeric claim attached. Excerpt and the node/edge wording correctly avoid naming SpaceX from this source. Agent flag (Linde never names SpaceX directly) CONFIRMED true for the primary source.

'Linde', 'SpaceX', 'Starbase', and '$100 million' all present. Sentence 2 near-verbatim with one comma difference: page reads 'liquid oxygen and nitrogen, essential for rocket launches, directly to SpaceX’s Starbase facility' whereas stored excerpt drops the second comma ('...rocket launches directly to...'). Air Liquide USA space page (vendor_marketing per ADR-0009 — valid for who-supplies-what role, weak for share/structure). Sentence verbatim in the Ground-systems section: 'supply liquid hydrogen and oxygen for the launch vehicles’ propulsion, liquid nitrogen for inerting, and the helium that is indispensable for pressurization, cool-down, and cleaning.' No numeric claim. SpaceX NOT named; page is Ariane/Kourou heritage ('360 cryogenic tanks since 1979', 'Ariane cryogenic launch complexes in Kourou') — consistent with the record being used for general launch-gas roles + Air Liquide capability, not a SpaceX contract. Supports the methane node only for the general launch-propulsion-fuels framing (page does not state a methane-supplier claim), as the limitations field already notes.

Nippon Sanso Matheson helium page (vendor_marketing). Both sentences verbatim: 'Nippon Sanso Matheson is one of only a handful of global producers and suppliers of helium.' and 'Nippon Sanso Matheson’s helium position is extremely strong and includes long term supply contracts with helium producers' (page continues '..., both foreign and domestic.'). Also confirmed on page: 'We own rights to helium sources in various parts of the world, complemented by a network of transfills.' No numeric claim. Space launch NOT mentioned (listed uses: welding, medical USP, MRI/NMR magnets, lasers, fiber-optic cooling, leak detection, weather balloons) — record is correctly used for the concentrated-helium-structure + Nippon Sanso role, a vendor self-description corroborated by USGS few-source structure; not a SpaceX-specific supply claim.

Messer (messer-us.com) corporate press release, fetched 200. All three constituent sentences verbatim: 'Messer, the largest privately held industrial gas company in the world...'; 'The Federal Helium System includes the Federal Helium Reserve, the Cliffside Field with its wells and gathering system, the 423-mile-long crude helium pipeline, and additional operational assets.'; 'Since April 2022, Messer has operated the Cliffside Gas Plant under contract with the BLM.' No market-share % stated on page (the ~15-17% secondary figure is correctly NOT used). GIC not mentioned on this page (GIC minority status is independently sourced — see ticker audit). Confirms Messer's private status and the Federal Helium System assets/Cliffside operation.

escalations.question: The Linde→SpaceX-customer identification for the Brownsville ASU rests ONLY on secondary sources (ConstructConnect trade press + City of Brownsville municipal release, both naming SpaceX/Starbase); Linde's own primary IR release (ev_space_linde_mims_2022) names the customer only as 'a major space launch company in Florida' and never says 'SpaceX'. The per-record quotes are all verified exact, and the brief's bar (§4.5) for a named-customer 'only/main-supplier' edge is 'one primary OR two independent quality sources'. Two independent secondaries (trade press + gov) do name SpaceX for Brownsville — does that satisfy the bar for the 'manufactured_by / SpaceX’s main industrial-gas supplier' edge framing, or should the edge be softened (e.g. relation downgraded / claim hedged to 'reported, per secondary sources') given no Linde-or-SpaceX primary confirms the SpaceX relationship? (Mims sub-claim is fine — it is correctly stated as 'major space launch company in Florida', matching the Linde primary.)
